newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lauda Air to increase Australia flights.
newsitem.headline: Lauda Air to increase Australia flights.

text.p: Austria's second largest airline, Lauda Air Luftfahrt AG, will expand its services to Melbourne and Sydney as part of a new Austria-Australia aviation pact, Federal Transport Minister John Sharp said on Tuesday.

"Negotiations concluded last week in Canberra with Austrian authorities to provide by October 1998 an 85 percent increase in seat capacity on passenger services for the airlines of both countries," Sharp said in a statement.
The new arrangements will permit Lauda Air to upgrade its service to Australia on October 1 this year by introducing its new Boeing Co B777 aircraft, he said.
"This upgrade by itself provides the potential for up to 40 percent more tourists per week for Melbourne," Sharp said.
He said benefits agreed on for both countries included opportunities for new air freight services and supplementary services to meet peak travel demands such as school holidays.

"Other benefits to flow from the new arrangements include new opportunities for Australian carriers such as Qantas (Airways Ltd ), which will be able to explore code share services to Vienna and beyond via a wider range of destinations in Europe," he said.
Sharp said Qantas started daily services to Vienna in July on a code share basis with its 25 percent shareholder, British Airways Plc.
